text:
crowfoot — a demo

This is the database behind nivoca, a Japanese vocabulary app.
The version drawn here is its legacy build: Next.js + Supabase, shipped as a PWA.
The app has since been rebuilt on Flutter with a Kotlin/Spring backend, and this
earlier codebase was opened as github.com/Junjak-Personal/nivoca-legacy.

23 tables · 27 foreign keys, parsed straight from 37 Supabase migration files:
    npx crowfoot erd build --input 'migrations/*.sql' --format postgres

Edit mode

Press Edit in the header — or add ?edit=1 to the URL. Without it the diagram is
read-only, so a link you share cannot be rearranged by whoever opens it.

Drag tables to move them. Drag across empty canvas to select several, and add to
that selection with Shift-click — Cmd-click on a Mac, Ctrl-click on Windows.
Whatever is selected moves, takes a colour and is deleted together.

Grouping

Select the tables you want and press Cmd/Ctrl + G. A named, tinted box is drawn
behind the members — it is derived from where they sit, so it follows them. Drag
the group label to move the whole set. Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + G ungroups, and asks
before it does.

A table may belong to more than one group. The toolbar switches between group
view and a plain alphabetical list without touching the data.

Memos and colour

Ctrl/Cmd + right-click empty canvas to drop a memo like this one. Memos resize,
recolour, change font size, and copy-paste — including into another browser tab.

Tables, memos and groups all take a tint from the same 12-colour palette, so the
diagram stays consistent with the app it documents.

Changing the schema

In edit mode the panel on the right becomes a form: a table's name, comment,
columns, keys, indexes and checks. Tables can be added and removed too.

Ctrl/Cmd + right-click a table, pick many : 1, 1 : 1, 1 : many or many : many,
then click the table to connect it to — many : many builds the join table.

Nothing here rearranges the diagram, and the DDL export reflects every edit.

Making an arrangement permanent

Your layout lives in the URL, which makes it shareable but not durable. Copy the
edit-mode URL and turn it into files the viewer loads on every visit:

    npx crowfoot erd from-link --input '<the URL>' --output-dir dist

That writes layout.json, memos.json and groups.json next to schema.json. Commit
them, and this arrangement is what everyone sees — this demo included.

Schema edits stay in the link on purpose. A diagram is a view of a real schema:
regenerate schema.json from the source rather than pinning an edited copy.

Where this runs

A static site: no server, no database connection. crowfoot parses the schema once
and emits HTML, CSS and JSON you can host anywhere — S3, nginx, GitHub Pages.
This page is nginx on a mini PC behind a Cloudflare tunnel.

The sidecar files and the script that generates them are in the repository under
demo/, so this arrangement survives the server it happens to be served from.

github.com/Junjak-Personal/crowfoot   ·   npm i -g crowfoot
